Definition: Bilhan, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite
BiblicalUsage: Bilhan means their decrepitude, and the name belongs to two men who must not be mixed up. Genesis 36:27 makes him a son of Ezer the Horite, the father of Akan — the Horite Akan of Genesis 36, not Achan of Joshua 7 — and 1 Chronicles 1:42 repeats the line. Then 1 Chronicles 7:10 names a different Bilhan, a Benjamite, the son of Jediael, whose sons are listed after him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two Bilhans are a warning to read slowly: same name, different men, and the difference matters.
